preserve is 67 % of the expected final part (133029 mm3 of 197221 mm3 at volfrac 0.05). Most of this shape is drawn, not optimised; say so wherever the result is presented.

the free region is only 2.0 voxels (6.00 mm) thick at its thinnest. Below about 3 voxels there is no room for a hole, so the topology there is set by the outline rather than chosen -- refine the grid or widen the design space.

the 6 support point(s) are fixed by preserve at knuckles at [-71.6, 9.8, 100.4]; latch_lo at [65.5, 7.5, 40.0]; latch_hi at [65.5, 7.5, 169.0]; pocket_bot at [-0.9, 40.4, -9.2]; band_mid at [-1.0, 39.2, 100.0]; pocket_top at [-1.3, 39.3, 207.0]. Where the part is held is an input to this study, not a result of it -- if the layout of the supports is itself meant to be optimised, that decision is currently being made in CAD.

printer.name: Bambu Lab X1-Carbon
printer.note: AMS-fed; the purge tower needs ~60x60 mm of plate on multi-material prints.

build_volume.voxel_vs_min_feature: one voxel is 3.00 mm and the smallest printable wall is 0.80 mm, so the grid cannot represent the printer's limit; minimum-feature checks on this run are about the grid, not the machine.

design_freedom.note_fixed_points: 11 load/support footprint(s) sit on preserve at positions the CAD model chose. The optimiser decides how to reach them, not where they are.

runtime_estimate.basis: one cold conjugate-gradient solve of load case 1 at uniform density, times cases times iterations. Warm starting makes later iterations cheaper; continuation towards a 0/1 field makes them dearer. Measured runs land within 0.5x - 1.5x.
